From 7425e8167507fe512d8ac0825acda4aebf0a7ca0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2021 15:40:05 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm: unlock on error in get_sched_entity()

Add a missing unlock on the error path if drm_sched_entity_init() fails.

Fixes: 68002469e571 ("drm/msm: One sched entity per process per priority")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211011124005.GE15188@kili
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@chromium.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
index b8621c6e0554..7cb158bcbcf6 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
@@ -101,6 +101,7 @@ get_sched_entity(struct msm_file_private *ctx, struct msm_ringbuffer *ring,
 
 		ret = drm_sched_entity_init(entity, sched_prio, &sched, 1, NULL);
 		if (ret) {
+			mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);
 			kfree(entity);
 			return ERR_PTR(ret);
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c`**
   - A line was added to unlock a mutex (`mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);`) in the error handling path of the `get_sched_entity` function. This occurs if the call to `drm_sched_entity_init(entity, sched_prio, &sched, 1, NULL);` fails (i.e., if `ret` is non-zero).
   - The line is placed before the cleanup of the `entity` object and the return of the error pointer.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where the mutex lock (`entity_lock`) was not being released if the initialization of the scheduling entity failed. This could lead to a deadlock situation, as the lock would remain held even when an error occurred. By adding the unlock operation in the error path, the patch ensures that the lock is properly released, maintaining the integrity of the locking mechanism and preventing potential deadlocks. This change is directly related to the previous commit identified by the fix tag, which introduced the scheduling entity logic.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
mutex_lock(&entity_lock);
ret = drm_sched_entity_init(entity, sched_prio, &sched, 1, NULL);
```
Reason:
The `mutex_lock(&entity_lock);` statement locks the mutex, but if `drm_sched_entity_init` fails (indicated by a non-zero `ret`), the subsequent code does not unlock the mutex before returning an error pointer. This results in the mutex remaining locked, which can lead to a deadlock situation if other threads attempt to acquire the same lock.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);
kfree(entity);
```
Reason:
The addition of `mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);` before returning the error pointer ensures that the mutex is released if `drm_sched_entity_init` fails. This prevents the potential deadlock by allowing other threads to acquire the lock, thus properly handling the error path in the function.
